Kudirkos Naumiestis Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Marijampolės apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Kudirkos Naumiestis — known in Yiddish as Nayshtot-Shaki — sits on Lithuania's border with what is now Russia's Kaliningrad region, and its Jewish community, settled in the mid-17th century, built much of its livelihood on cross-border trade and even the smuggling of migrants into Germany. Rising Nazi persecution in neighboring Germany closed the border and devastated the local economy well before the war reached Lithuania itself. Nearly 800 Jews lived here in 1941; all were murdered that year — Jewish men were shot directly at this cemetery in July 1941, and women and children were killed at the Paražnai forest that September. Only one woman and her four children, sheltered by Lithuanian peasants, survived. The cemetery, likely established in the early 18th century, was neglected but not built upon during the Soviet era; besides Jewish victims, it also became a killing and burial site for other victims of Nazi rule, including Soviet soldiers, commemorated by a separate monument erected in 2011.
